Serial and parallel mediators, and sampling weights, with the native engine. Part
of the [Models](models.html) collection; the last of four
[native engine](model-native.html) pages. The engine is experimental.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Structure** | serial (a chain) or parallel mediators written as syntax |
| **Route** | `fit_sem()`, then `extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c(...), outcome = )` |
| **Classes returned** | `SerialMediationData` or `ParallelMediationData` |
| **Weights** | `fit_sem(weights = , se_type = "sandwich")` |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Not `fit_mediation(engine = "native")`
`fit_mediation(engine = "native")` takes **one** mediator and stops with "Must have
length 1" for more. For several, fit with `fit_sem()` and extract.
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
covs <- "covariate1 + covariate2"
```

## Serial mediators

```{r}
#| label: serial
serial_syntax <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + b1 * mediator1 + cp * treatment + ", covs)
sfit <- fit_sem(serial_syntax, mediation_demo)
xs <- extract_mediation(sfit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        outcome = "outcome")
class(xs)[1]
c(chain = unname(nie(xs)), every_path = unname(nie(xs, type = "total")),
  total = unname(te(xs)))
```

With the default `structure = "auto"`, medfit classifies the mediators from the
model: here it finds the path from `mediator1` to `mediator2` and returns the
serial class. See [Serial mediation](model-serial.html) for what the three
numbers mean.

## Parallel mediators

```{r}
#| label: parallel
parallel_syntax <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a1 * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator2 ~ a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b1 * mediator1 + b2 * mediator2 + cp * treatment + ", covs)
pfit <- fit_sem(parallel_syntax, mediation_demo)
xp <- extract_mediation(pfit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        outcome = "outcome", structure = "parallel")
class(xp)[1]
tidy(xp, type = "effects", conf.int = TRUE)
```

## Sampling weights

`weights` gives weighted maximum likelihood; pair it with
`se_type = "sandwich"` for robust standard errors. The weights below are random,
only to show the call:

```{r}
#| label: weights
set.seed(1)
w <- runif(nrow(mediation_demo), 0.5, 2)
wsyntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  ab := a * b
"
wfit <- fit_sem(wsyntax, mediation_demo, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
wfit@defined
```

The scale of the weights does not matter. Supplying weights with the default
`se_type = "model"` prints a once-per-session message that model-based standard
errors are not valid under inverse-probability weighting.

## Limits

- **`fit_mediation(engine = "native")` takes one mediator** (see the warning above).
- **No four-way decomposition and no mean structure** from the native engine.
- **The native sandwich is the HC0 type**, with casewise scores; the `glm`
  engine's sandwich is HC3. They are different estimators, so the standard errors
  need not match.
- **The sandwich treats observations as independent**, so it does not handle
  survey clusters, strata or replicate weights.
